name: JARRETT, Madonna

headline.note: Official parliamentary and candidate material establishes radiography, NSW and Queensland government advisory work and a long Deloitte career, but does not publish the hours, leave or complete employment boundaries required for a full-time duration calculation. Political staff work and elected office are excluded. Deloitte titles and month-level sequencing are partly supported by public professional-profile aggregations and contemporary Deloitte publications, but full-time status and the initial and final payroll dates remain unresolved. Missing evidence is not zero.

career_spells.role: Bachelor of Business and Diploma of Applied Science (Diagnostic Radiography) student
career_spells.evidence_note: The official parliamentary biography lists both QUT qualifications but no attendance or completion dates.

The official biography records work as a radiographer and the ALP biography says Jarrett started her career in health. Employer, jurisdiction, dates, hours, leave and public/private control are not published.
career_spells.counting_note: Neither sector nor a bounded full-time interval is established.

career_spells.employer: NSW and Queensland government ministerial offices not identified
career_spells.evidence_note: The official biography records advisory work for NSW and Queensland governments. ABC and AAP profiles add that Jarrett worked as an adviser and chief of staff to state ministers and was a policy adviser during the Wayne Goss government. The offices, employing entities, dates, hours and leave remain unpublished.
career_spells.counting_note: Political staff employment is excluded irrespective of public funding.

career_spells.role: Global public relations / chief-executive communications role
career_spells.evidence_note: Jarrett's ALP biography describes a 25-year private-sector career. Contemporary Deloitte releases identify her as global director of public relations and chief-executive communications in January 2006 and continue to list her as a Deloitte media contact in 2007 and 2008. A public professional-profile aggregation places the next Deloitte program-lead role from September 2010. The original Deloitte commencement date, legal employing entity, hours and leave are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Contemporary sources establish private employment by 2006, but the unbounded start and missing full-time evidence prevent counting.

career_spells.role: Program Lead, Global Regulatory and Public Policy Group / Global Public Policy Group
career_spells.evidence_note: A public professional-profile aggregation reports Global Regulatory and Public Policy program leadership from September 2010 to October 2014 and Global Public Policy program leadership from October 2014 to September 2017. A 2017 IOE/Deloitte report independently identifies Jarrett as a Director of Deloitte Belgium and the Deloitte Global Public Policy Group, corroborating employer and function but not the full month sequence or hours.
career_spells.counting_note: Month-level role sequencing is useful evidence, but full-time status, leave and payroll continuity are not established.

career_spells.role: Acting Chief of Staff, then Chief of Staff, Global Risk and Regulatory / Public Policy leadership
career_spells.evidence_note: Public professional-profile aggregations report Acting Chief of Staff from September 2017 to June 2018 and Chief of Staff from June 2018 to January 2019. A 2018 Deloitte-supported report independently identifies Jarrett as a director in Deloitte's Global Risk and Regulatory Group in Belgium, corroborating the organisation and senior global-risk function but not payroll conditions.
career_spells.counting_note: The sources do not establish full-time status, leave or uninterrupted employment across the title transition.

career_spells.role: Director, Global Risk and Global Regulatory and Public Policy
career_spells.evidence_note: The official parliamentary biography confirms Deloitte employment. ABC's 2022 and 2025 election guides identify Jarrett's most recent role as a Deloitte Australia director responsible for global risk and regulatory/public policy. A public professional-profile aggregation gives January 2019 as the start, and news profiles report her return to Australia in 2019 after about 15 years overseas. The end is bounded by federal election day rather than a sourced payroll date; hours, leave and any campaign arrangement are unknown.
career_spells.counting_note: A substantial private-sector spell is supported, but the project does not infer full-time status from a director title or election transition.

career_spells.evidence_note: A candidate interview identifies Jarrett as a volunteer board member of Brisbane homelessness charity 3rd Space. Dates and any remuneration are not reported.
career_spells.counting_note: Volunteer governance is excluded from substantive employment totals.

career_spells.evidence_note: Official parliamentary service begins with the 3 May 2025 federal election.

research_notes: Identify the radiography employer, dates, hours and whether it was publicly or privately controlled.

Identify each NSW and Queensland ministerial office, employing entity, title, appointment/cessation, hours and leave; confirm whether any role was public-service employment rather than political staff.

Obtain a primary Deloitte appointment history: original commencement, legal employing entities, movements between Australia and Belgium, exact title boundaries, hours, leave and final cessation or campaign arrangement.

The public professional-profile aggregations provide useful month-level leads but are not treated as proof of full-time status or uninterrupted payroll service. Seek archived Deloitte biographies, annual reports and conference profiles.

Resolve whether any other paid employment occurred between radiography, government advisory work and Deloitte, and distinguish public affairs or crisis-management consulting from internal Deloitte roles.
